subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required?
rationale: The unresolved scope can expose filesystem, process, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the supported product boundary or security model.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs with explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare current HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron support sufficient, then close or reject host-FS, exec, slash, and CLI direct dispatch until a maintainer sponsors a narrower proposal.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only after a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs with explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the direct-invoke security boundary, and this owner has recent history on /tools/invoke operator-boundary and gateway-tool behavior.
